task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-05-23, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
If PNR fail then PULL_UP is a real league-wide counter, it should show lift>0 in >=70% of units with median lift>2pp.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: PULL_UP as a counter to a failed PNR
lift in percentage points versus a within-unit baseline
share of units with lift>0 (>=70%) and median lift >2pp
methodological_questions: How is a PNR fail defined from play-by-play without using the outcome that PULL_UP lift is measured on?
What is the comparator for PULL_UP: other continuations after the same failed PNR, or the unit's general PULL_UP rate?
Is there enough PULL_UP-after-fail exposure per unit for a sign-share criterion to be meaningful?
Would the 70%/2pp rule be passed by sampling noise, regression to the mean or a mechanical floor?
Which confounders (shooter quality, clock, score, matchup, PNR proxy label error) could produce lift without a counter effect?
Does the pattern replicate across seasons, or is it a one-season artifact?

historical_evidence.finding: The A1 adaptation falsification (asymmetry, confidence and carryover tests) found an apparent adapter PPP lift (+0.0667, n=205). But no-signal teams had +0.1260 (n=57) and wrong-way teams +0.0111 (n=274). Adapter minus no-signal was negative (-0.0361 with 1 vote, -0.1170 with 2 votes), and next-game carryover was not significant (Welch t=-1.003, p=0.842). Recorded failure mechanism: C_artifact (a construction, selection or labelling flaw). Limited by selection/regression to the mean and label/classification error. Risks listed: LABEL_ERROR, MECHANICAL_FLOOR.

Within-game adaptation toward 'SHOULD' counter play types showed adapter advantages of about +0.048 to +0.058 PPP. The SWITCH subgroup reversed (-0.0436 or -0.0160), and the no-signal baseline had the highest dPPP. Recorded as limited by selection or regression to the mean.

Within-scheme re-test controlling for early-PPP selection: the adapter-minus-wrong-way gap was DROP +0.0830 (p=0.0046), HELP +0.0539 (p=0.0493) and SWITCH -0.0199 (p=0.6514). The quintile gaps were inconsistent in sign (-0.0440, -0.0231, +0.0138, +0.0133, +0.0966). The carryover gap for DROP was +0.0039 (p=0.4244). Failure mechanism recorded as E_unclear.

Descriptive shot-level PNR share of half-court shots in 2024-25 ranged from OKC 7.567% to IND 13.824%. [prior work] says these are calibration inputs for a PBP proxy PNR detector. Later logs show calibrated PNR at about 17.9-19.6% of possessions. No validation was recorded.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Treating a positive PPP lift for teams that shifted toward 'counter' play types as evidence of a real coverage response
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as an artifact: the no-signal baseline was higher than the adapters', wrong-way teams were not worse, and carryover was null. Limited by selection/regression to the mean and by label error.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Within-game did_adapt comparison of adapters against non-adapters
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as artifact, limited by selection/regression to the mean. The effect was heterogeneous by scheme (SWITCH reversed).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Within-scheme and early-PPP-quintile control as a fix for selection
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as inconclusive with an unclear mechanism. The effect appeared only in some schemes and the quintile gaps changed sign.

evidence_establishes: No retrieved record tests PULL_UP specifically as a counter after a failed PNR, or a share-of-units criterion like >=70% with lift>0.

Earlier counter and adaptation analyses by this project were recorded as artifact ([prior work][prior work], FAM:[prior work]) or inconclusive (FAM:[prior work]), with selection/regression to the mean and label error as the recorded limitations.
Earlier counter-lift effects were heterogeneous across schemes, with the SWITCH subgroup reversing sign, so league-wide uniformity is not supported by [prior work].
PBP-derived PNR labels were only calibrated against shot-level rates, with no validation recorded ([prior work][prior work]).
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether PULL_UP has positive lift after a failed PNR in any unit or season.
Whether the PNR-fail label can be built without an outcome-derived component.
The per-unit exposure counts for PULL_UP after a PNR fail.
Whether any lift persists out of sample or across seasons.
Whether the proxy PNR detector is accurate enough to define 'fail'.
own_inferences: The hypothesis is largely a sign-consistency test. With noisy small per-unit samples, the true null of zero lift would give about 50% of units positive. Passing 70% needs either a real broad effect or bias, so power per unit and a placebo distribution of the sign share are essential.

If 'fail' is defined by a low-value result such as a missed shot, turnover or no shot, then the next-action outcome is mechanically tied to the label (MECHANICAL_FLOOR, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL). That can inflate or deflate PULL_UP lift.

A pull-up is typically a lower-efficiency shot type (more mid-range) than rim or 3 attempts. A median lift above +2pp against a pooled alternative may therefore be unlikely unless the baseline is chosen carefully, or fail possessions are defined by late-clock states where pull-ups are forced.
Selection of who pulls up (better shooters, late clock, scoring situations) may drive any apparent lift without any causal counter effect.
The 'best/avoid' framing also invites a reading of 'avoid' for non-qualifying units, so a pre-registered null interpretation is needed.
uncertainties: The definition of PNR fail and of PULL_UP in the derived play-type records is not given in the task and is not documented in the retrieved records.
The unit is not specified (team-season, player-season, or team-opponent).
The 2025-26 playoffs were partial on the posting date 2026-05-23, and the full-season data are only complete later.
Unknown PBP proxy PNR precision and recall.
No earlier PULL_UP-specific record was returned, and I did not read the full family texts (several fields are cut).

historical_effect.explanation: Without history I would have been inclined to proceed with a plain unit sign-share test. [prior work] show that similar counter-lift tests were artifacts of selection, regression to the mean, label error and mechanical floors, and had scheme-dependent sign reversals. So I require a placebo-calibrated sign-share test, an outcome-independent PNR-fail label, within-unit comparators and cross-season replication, and I lower the prior probability of 'supported'.

blocking_constraints.text: If PNR 'fail' is defined from the possession outcome, PULL_UP lift is partly mechanical. Fail must be defined from process features (such as no rim attempt, no drive or no pass within N seconds, or a defender-contested state) that precede the PULL_UP decision.
PULL_UP-after-fail counts per unit may be very small, so unit-level sign would be mostly noise. Units below a pre-set minimum must be excluded or pooled.
PNR and PULL_UP labels come from the derived play-by-play proxy with no recorded validation ([prior work][prior work]). Label noise can bias lift toward zero or create spurious team differences.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved family tests PULL_UP as a counter after a failed PNR. Adjacent adaptation and counter families were recorded as artifact or inconclusive, with selection/regression to the mean and label error as limitations. The PNR proxy is only calibrated, not validated.

risks.text: A fail label tied to the outcome makes next-action results mechanically correlated with it.
Failed-PNR possessions start from a depressed state, so any following action looks better or worse by construction.
Teams and players selected on poor PNR results regress toward their means, and units with more pull-ups are self-selected.
Per-unit samples are small, so the sign share is noisy, and a 70% threshold with a 2pp median is hard to power.
PULL_UP after fail is a rare conditional event for many units.
Shooter quality, shot clock, score, defender and coverage, and who initiates all drive pull-up efficiency.
The proxy PNR and PULL_UP labels are unvalidated, with no recorded validation ([prior work][prior work]).
Several unit definitions, thresholds, seasons and comparators could be tried until the 70%/2pp criterion is met.
Season-to-season changes in pull-up rates and coverages, with 2025-26 partly incomplete on the posting date.
Pull-up shot types have a different efficiency baseline from rim or 3 attempts, so lift against pooled alternatives is confounded with shot type.

design.estimand: For each unit, the within-unit difference in points per possession (and in eFG as a secondary measure) between possessions where a PULL_UP follows a failed PNR and matched possessions where another pre-specified action follows the same failed PNR state. The league-level quantities are the share of eligible units with lift>0 and the median unit lift in pp. A 'real counter' needs both, with the share >=70% and the median >2pp, and the share must also exceed what the placebo distribution gives.
design.unit: Team-season offense (the ball-handling side), for each of the four complete or near-complete season blocks. A player-ball-handler-season analysis is secondary with a minimum exposure rule.
design.sample: 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25 regular seasons are the discovery and confirmation sets. The 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13) is the held-out confirmation set. Playoffs are excluded from the primary test. The 2025-26 playoffs were partial on 2026-05-23 and are excluded entirely. Eligible units need at least N_min failed-PNR possessions with a PULL_UP continuation and N_min with an alternative continuation. N_min is set from a power calculation before looking at outcomes, for example 40 each.
design.power: Before analysis, simulate the sign share using the observed per-unit exposure counts and PPP variance (about 1.0-1.2 per possession). Compute the share of units positive under a true common lift of 0pp and of 2pp. If power to distinguish 70% from the 50% null is below about 0.8 given the number of eligible units (around 30 per season, up to about 120 across seasons), report the test as underpowered and use pooled or partial-pooling estimates instead of the sign share.
design.controls: Define PNR fail from the process, not the outcome: no rim attempt, no foul and no open-shot creation within a fixed window after the screen, based on the clock and event sequence. Define PULL_UP from the shot sub-type and distance. Control for shot clock, score margin, period, shooter identity or shooter shot-making baseline (shrunk), defender matchup, and opponent coverage proxy. Use within-unit comparison and shrink unit estimates by empirical Bayes to limit RTM. Validate the proxy PNR and PULL_UP labels on a hand-checked sample before the main run and report precision.
design.falsification: (1) Placebo: apply the same procedure to randomly assigned fake fail labels and to non-PNR possessions matched on clock and score; the placebo sign-share distribution defines the null. (2) Reversed-timing test: the label must be set before the continuation is observed, so a lookahead shift should not change it. (3) Split-half stability: lift by unit in season A must predict season B above the placebo. (4) Alternative comparators: check against a catch-and-shoot or rim-attempt continuation to detect a shot-type base-rate effect. (5) Check that the effect does not depend on the fail-definition threshold.
design.multiplicity: One primary hypothesis (sign share >=70% and median >2pp), one primary comparator, one fail definition and one unit definition, all fixed before looking at outcomes. Secondary analyses (player units, alternative thresholds, eFG) are labelled exploratory and corrected with Holm or reported as descriptive.
design.decision_rule: Supported only if, in discovery and in the held-out 2025-26 regular season separately: the share of eligible units with lift>0 is >=70% and exceeds the 95th percentile of the placebo share; the median lift is >2pp with a bootstrap CI excluding 0; and the lift is positive after controls. Rejected if the CI for the median lift or the share lies adequately below the thresholds with adequate power. If the effect disappears under controls, the placebo or the alternative comparator, label it artifact. If power is inadequate, report it as untestable or inconclusive and make no 'best/avoid' claim.
design.data_version: Freeze play-by-play and derived play-type records as of the analysis date. Seasons 2022-23 to 2024-25 are complete, the 2025-26 regular season is complete from 2026-04-13 (use only after that date), and exclude the 2025-26 playoffs (partial until 2026-06-21). Record the derived-graph build version and label-definition hash with the registration.
